points.quote: Its extensions are simply its `dependencies`, such as `@theia/ai-chat` and `@theia/editor`. ... `theia build` (from `@theia/cli`, implemented in `dev-packages/application-manager`)
It declares its entry points in `package.json` under `theiaExtensions`.
`src/browser` is the frontend, `src/node` is the backend, and `src/common` is shared. (frontend/backend keys shown; no frontendElectron/backendElectron fallback rule)
That module exports an InversifyJS `ContainerModule`, which binds the extension's services and contributions.

An extension adds behavior by binding contribution interfaces, such as `CommandContribution`, `MenuContribution` ... Core collects them through `ContributionProvider`. (does not name @theia/core as the main extension every app builds on)
`src/electron-browser` and `src/electron-main` cover Electron. (omits browser-only, electron-node and the restriction that browser/node may use only common)
Its `theia` field holds the config: `frontend.config` (application name, default preferences) and `backend.config`. (no target browser/electron)

`theia start` (or `npm run start:browser`) runs the generated backend. ... In Electron, the main process runs the backend and the renderer runs the frontend. (generation and esbuild covered; no localhost:3000, and the Electron subprocess fork is not stated)
